lectures.title: The OpenAI API & SDK Is The Industry Standard

cues.en: Now for this section,
we'll focus on the API
provided by OpenAI, and we'll explore how we
can use their models through their
API. Now, as I mentioned in the last
lecture, you can also use other services
like OpenRouter to access all kinds of models
from all kinds of providers through an API,
and take a look at their documentation to learn how to do
that. And, of course, you could also
go for the APIs provided by Google or
xAI to access the APIs of
their own AI models. That is
all up to you. We will focus on the
OpenAI APIs though, not
just because ChatGPT started it all
and to this day is arguably the most
important and popular AI
model and AI chatbot, but also because
the OpenAI
SDK, the software
development kit, which is a package that simplifies
the process of integrating these APIs
into your applications, this OpenAI
SDK became the de facto
standard for many of those
AI API providers. So what you'll
learn in this section about this SDK will
also help you with using the APIs by
some other providers because other
providers, like for example, Google,
offer support for the OpenAI
SDK, which means that you actually are
able to use the OpenAI SDK, which
we will cover in this section, to
interact with APIs by some other
providers, because this OpenAI SDK
allows you to specify something called the base
URL, which in the end simply tells
this software package provided by OpenAI
under the hood to which behind the scenes
provider it should connect. And that provider
can be swapped from OpenAI, which would be the
default, to any kind of provider like, for example,
Google, if that provider supports it, which
many providers do. So that's why
learning about the OpenAI SDK makes a lot of
sense, because what you learn will not just help you
with using the OpenAI APIs
through that SDK, but potentially also
other APIs by other providers.
